name: American nationalism
summary: American nationalism holds that Americans are one nation, represented by the US government, whose independence, union and identity are to be defended. It runs from the founders' union and neutrality through Lincoln's creedal nation and Theodore Roosevelt's demand for undivided allegiance to restrictionist and America First nationalism, which differ on immigration, religion and ethnicity.
scope: The American nation as such: its union, identity, territory, sovereignty, language, culture, membership and loyalty, from Washington, Jay, Jackson, Lincoln, Theodore Roosevelt and Lodge to Reagan's patriotism and Trump's America First. The wider programmes of the parties and administrations that carried it (economy, welfare, social policy) are left out unless the nationalist texts state them as part of the national cause. Contemporary national-conservative texts could not be opened (see notes). White-nationalist and separatist movements are not the mainstream.
